title: Traumatic brain injury disease-modifying treatment
bottleneck: TBI spans concussion to severe injury with heterogeneous pathology, including contusion, diffuse axonal injury, and hemorrhage, and no drug has been shown to improve outcomes; trials fail on heterogeneity, insensitive endpoints, and poor preclinical models.
why_it_blocks: TBI is a leading cause of death and disability in young adults, and repeated mild TBI is linked to chronic traumatic encephalopathy; supportive care has barely changed in decades.
current_state: Blood biomarkers such as GFAP and UCH-L1 now aid diagnosis and trial enrichment, and several candidates are in trials. No disease-modifying TBI therapy exists. The heterogeneity of TBI, from concussion to severe injury, means no single therapy will fit all patients. Better classification by biomarker and imaging endotype is a prerequisite for successful trials, and the field is only now building that foundation.
